title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two Rio Arriba County sisters are suing the city of Española over a July 23 traffic stop. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, and her 12-year-old sister were pulled over on Calle Duran after a Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, reading a final 2 as 7 and flagging the car as stolen from Rio Rancho. Officers handcuffed both sisters and placed them in separate police cars before realizing the error. Jaclynn asked police to call their nearby mother to pick up the girl, but officers instead handcuffed the 12-year-old and put her in another vehicle.

The lawsuits, filed January 3, seek unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restriction of movement. Attorney Sheri Raphaelson also filed a similar case in April for Adam Pacheco, then 17, who was forced to kneel with his hands on his head after being wrongly linked to an armed robbery. The city, police chief, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. No next steps are stated beyond the pending lawsuits.
